name: God’s Decrees and Sovereignty
path: Theology Proper: The Doctrine of God

objectives.text: Identify God as the King who rules over all things
Retell how Jesus says God feeds the birds and clothes the flowers to describe God's care for his creation
Recall from Scripture that nothing happens by chance apart from God, not even the fall of a sparrow
Retell the story of Joseph and explain how God used his brothers' evil actions for good
Define providence as God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing of all his creatures and all their actions
Explain from Scripture that God rules over both good times and hard times
Compare the idea of luck or chance with the biblical teaching of providence
Explain how Nebuchadnezzar's confession in Daniel shows God's rule over kings and nations
Explain how the Reformed confessions describe the comfort that the doctrine of providence offers believers in suffering
Define God's decree as his eternal purpose according to the counsel of his will by which he has foreordained whatever comes to pass
Explain how God carries out his decrees in the works of creation and providence
Distinguish God's secret decretive will from his revealed moral will using passages that teach each
Analyze how the apostles' preaching about the cross holds together God's definite plan and the real guilt of those who crucified Jesus
Explain the Reformed teaching that God's decree establishes rather than removes the liberty of creatures and the working of second causes, and that God is not the author of sin
Explain the doctrines of election and predestination as taught in Paul's letters and the Reformed confessions
Interpret Romans 9 within Paul's argument about God's faithfulness to Israel, including his use of Malachi on Jacob and Esau
Explain the Reformed teaching that election is unconditional and not based on foreseen faith or works
Explain how the Reformed confessions state the doctrine of reprobation and why they urge that it be handled with special prudence and care
Construct a structured summary of the doctrine of the decrees that traces God's eternal purpose through its execution in creation, providence, and redemption
Evaluate the Arminian and Reformed views of election by testing each against key biblical passages
Evaluate major responses to the problem of evil and defend the goodness of God as the Reformed tradition confesses it
Create a written argument showing how Scripture presents God's sovereignty as a basis for evangelism and prayer rather than a reason to neglect them

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (God as King, providence, Joseph, luck versus providence, sovereign versus moral will, Romans 9, compatibilism, election, decrees, Arminian versus Reformed, evil, evangelism and prayer). Dropped the near-duplicate 'one who decides what happens' and replaced 'apply trust in God's plan', an inner-experience goal, with explaining the comfort the confessions attach to providence. Added objectives on Daniel 4 and God's rule over nations, the definition of the decree, how God executes his decrees, the cross in Acts as a case of sovereignty and responsibility, unconditional election, and reprobation as confessed with its caution. Moved the decree definition to grade 7, the reading of Romans 9 to grade 10, and placed Romans 9 within Paul's argument about Israel. Corrected confession citations to the standard document names and added Heidelberg Catechism, Canons of Dort, and further Westminster references where they state the doctrine.
